newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy stocks drift down, absorbing ERM and Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Italy stocks drift down, absorbing ERM and Prodi.

text.p: Italian stocks drifted to a lower close on Monday as euphoria over the lira's ERM entry soon wore off to be replaced by worries over its effect on exporters and concern over a possible trial of prime minister Romano Prodi.

News that a Rome magistrate was seeking a trial for Prodi over abuse of office when he was head of state industrial holding IRI momentarily rattled the share market, but Prodi said he had faith in the Italian judicial system. Dealers said firmer bonds and a higher Wall Street failed to encourage share buying.
The all-share Mibtel index ended off 0.48 percent to 10,492 while the Mib30 blue chip closed down 0.68 percent at 15,680.

Dealers said that stocks reacted cautiously to the ERM parity rate of 990 lire/mark, slightly stronger than the 1,000 lire rate Italy was looking for, and some big industrial exporter stocks were marked down in response.
Although some dealers believed the strong rate would act as a further break on inflationary pressures and generally help the stocks market to eventually higher levels.

Industrial giant Fiat ended off 1.4 percent at 4,580 lire, tyre and cables group Pirelli was down 0.76 percent at 2,765 percent with information technology company Olivetti easing 1.11 percent to 561.0 lire.

The insurance sector was again of interest with SAI one of the few stocks to rise, up 1.01 percent at 13,975 lire, on continued takeover talk with the group still to announce a new chairman and managing director. Generali rumoured to be interested in SAI was off 2.89 percent at 30,200 lire.
